BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

IN THE MATTER OF SOUTHWESTERN PUBLIC )
SERVICE COMPANY’S APPLICATION FOR: (1) )
REVISION OF ITS RETAIL RATES UNDER ADVICE )                                  Docket No. 25-00079-UT
NOTICE 341; AND (2) OTHER ASSOCIATED RELIEF. )


                          STAFF’S MOTION FOR ORAL ARGUMENT

        COMES NOW the Utility Division Staff (“Staff”) of the New Mexico Public Regulation

Commission (“Commission”), in accordance with 1.2.2.12 NMAC, 1 and moves the Commission

for an order allowing oral argument on the Certification of Stipulation issued on October 23, 2026

(“Certification” or “Cert.”).

        1.      Presently, the Commission must decide whether to adopt the Certification of a

contested stipulation where Staff is the only contesting party. Staff’s decision not to sign the

Stipulation is based upon its statutory duty to represent the public interest and to ensure that the

end result of a general rate case is the setting of fair, just and reasonable rates. Oral argument

would assist the Commission decide the contested legal issues and is in the public interest.

        2.      Staff seeks to offer oral argument on the following issue: Has Southwestern Public

Service Company (“SPS”) fulfilled its burden of proof that the Contested Stipulation results in

fair, just and reasonable rates and is in accordance with law where: a) the revenue requirement is

based upon stale linkage data? b) the jurisdictional allocation between Texas and New Mexico has

not been adjusted for differences in test periods between the two states and will cause

overcollection of the jurisdictional allocation of the revenue requirement from New Mexico



1

"[t]he commission discourages any delay in the filing of a motion once grounds for the motion are known to the
movant.”

 customers? As this issue is, at least at this point in the adjudicatory process, legal rather than factual

in nature, oral argument would assist the Commission in rendering a final decision.

          3.      Section 62-19-20(C) provides: “When the commission has appointed a hearing

examiner to preside over a matter, at least one member of the commission shall, at the request of

a party to the proceedings, attend oral argument.”

          4.      Precedent establishes that the Commission will order oral argument where it may

facilitate the resolution of contested legal issues or is otherwise in the public interest:

      •   Case No. 15-00261-UT: 2 The Commission granted New Energy Economy’s Motion for
          Oral Argument allowing oral argument on remand from the New Mexico Supreme Court.

      •   Case No. 15-00127-UT: 3 The Commission granted Vote Solar’s Motion for Oral Argument
          to the Commission on its pending appeal of the Hearing Examiner’s order denying motions
          for interlocutory appeal of the denial of motions to dismiss E1 Paso Electric Company’s
          rate case.

      •   Case No. 24-00269-UT: 4 The Hearing Examiners ordered an oral argument by notifying
          “[t]he attorneys participating in the hearing … that they will be asked to offer a brief oral
          argument at the conclusion of the evidentiary portion of the hearing… This oral argument
          is intended to allow the attorneys to argue, and the hearing examiners to ask questions
          about, the law surrounding this aspect of the case.”


          5.      Staff has contacted the other parties in this case and at the time of this filing Staff

is authorized to state: SPS opposes and CCAE does not oppose.
